title: Post-SOW Implementation Readiness & KPI Baseline Survey
lede: A structured instrument issued to customer decision makers after SOW signature and before kickoff. It does two jobs at once: it measures whether the organization is actually ready to absorb a new vendor and a new operating model, and it captures a defensible current-state KPI baseline that seeds the post-go-live optimization program.

meta.Green: 4.0 – 5.0 — Proceed as scoped. Note the dimension in the kickoff deck and move on.
meta.Amber: 3.0 – 3.9 — Named mitigation with an owner and a date, agreed at kickoff.
meta.Red: Below 3.0 — Raise before kickoff. May warrant a schedule or scope conversation.

questions.text: Describe anything in today's environment that absolutely must not break during migration.
We have accurate, current documentation of our existing call flows and routing logic.
Which product does each department consume?
prompts: list the customer's actual departments here — e.g. Sales, Support, Billing, Scheduling, Clinical intake, Front office, Field ops, Back office, IT helpdesk, Executive
questions.logic: Customize prompts per engagement from the SOW. This single question replaces several separate multi-selects and produces a cleaner coverage matrix.

questions.text: Which channels does each department handle today, and which should it handle at go-live?
questions.logic: The today-versus-tomorrow delta per channel is the single most useful sizing input for the CX build, and it exposes channels the customer intends to add that the SOW may not cover.

questions.text: Rank the order in which sites or departments should go live.
questions.logic: Rows = sites or departments; columns = wave 1 through wave N. Reveals sequencing disagreements between stakeholders before design starts.

questions.text: Every impacted department has a named representative committed to design and UAT sessions.
Name the representative for each department or site you listed.
Which groups have not yet been briefed on this change?
Front-line staff and leadership agree on why we are changing platforms.
Do any third parties (BPO, answering service, MSP, after-hours vendor) touch these call flows?
In your own words: what does success look like 90 days after go-live?
questions.logic: Highest-signal question in the instrument. Divergence across respondents here is the single best predictor of a contested go-live.

questions.text: What are the three biggest problems with your current solution?
Rank these outcomes by priority for your organization.
For each process area, what should happen in the new platform?
questions.logic: Directly sizes design effort. A wall of "Redesign from scratch" against a SOW scoped for lift-and-shift is a change order conversation, not a surprise in week six.

questions.text: Our team has a shared, documented picture of the future-state experience we are building.
We are prepared to change business process, not only technology, to reach our goals.
questions.logic: Feeds both the Readiness Index and the optimization program. A low score here caps what optimization can deliver.

questions.text: What would make this project a failure in your eyes?
What do you believe is included in what we signed?
questions.logic: Scored against the SOW, not graded for correctness. Every mismatch between what a decision maker believes was bought and what was actually signed is a change-order or trust conversation you want at kickoff rather than at UAT. Split across two matching questions if your tenant caps prompt count.

questions.logic: "No" or "Unknown" triggers an immediate action item: request the export before the incumbent contract lapses. Historical data is frequently lost at cutover and cannot be recovered.

questions.logic: Makes delegation explicit instead of producing guessed answers. Anything unselected becomes a named follow-up rather than a silent gap.

questions.logic: Concurrency, not monthly volume, is what sizes the deployment. Ask for it explicitly — customers reliably volunteer volume and omit concurrency.

questions.text: Basis for the concurrency figures above:
options: Derived from Erlang or WFM modelling
questions.logic: A guessed concurrency number carried into sizing is one of the more expensive errors available. Anything below "measured" gets validated against reporting before design sign-off.

questions.text: Growth headroom to size for over the next 24 months:
Describe your peak: time of day, day of week, seasonal pattern, and the largest single-day spike in the last twelve months.
How should each channel be staffed at go-live?
questions.logic: Blending intent drives skill design, concurrency limits per agent and WFM complexity. Customers who say "blended" without having run blended before need that flagged early.

questions.text: Do you have a formal service target per channel today?
Is there a channel you want customers to move away from, or toward? Describe the shift you want and why.
questions.logic: Sets the deflection thesis for the optimization program. "We want voice volume into chat and self-service" is a measurable goal; without it, containment targets are arbitrary.

How does your current platform define these metrics where it may differ from the standard? Call out your short-abandon threshold, whether after-call work is included in handle time, whether abandons count against service level, and how first contact resolution is determined.
questions.logic: The most valuable free-text field in the instrument. Without it, every post-go-live comparison is contestable.

groups.title: Digital channel baseline — email, SMS, social, web chat

questions.text: Reporting availability per digital channel.
questions.logic: Gate B4.2–B4.6 on this. Digital reporting is far weaker than voice reporting at most customers, and pretending otherwise produces a baseline nobody will defend.

Social surfaces in scope:
questions.logic: Public comment moderation and private messaging are different problems with different owners. Separating them here prevents a scope gap in week three.

questions.text: Who handles social today?
questions.logic: If the answer is marketing, you have a second stakeholder group that has not been in any project meeting yet. Add them to A5.

questions.text: Describe how email reaches an agent today — shared mailboxes, aliases, case system, auto-acknowledgement rules — and what must be preserved.
questions.logic: Email migration is consistently underestimated. Shared-mailbox sprawl and forwarding rules are where it goes wrong.

questions.text: SMS number strategy:
questions.logic: Messaging registration (10DLC, toll-free verification) has lead time measured in weeks and is a common late-discovery go-live blocker. Start it at kickoff.

prompts: Preview (agent reviews the record before dialing)
Progressive (dials as an agent becomes available)
questions.logic: Include the plain-language definition in each prompt. Customers routinely select "Power" meaning "fast," and the pacing, compliance and staffing implications are entirely different.

questions.text: Describe each outbound campaign you run or plan to run: purpose, list size, frequency, and which mode it needs.

What do you dial with today?
Which compliance regimes apply to your outbound?
questions.logic: "None known" on an outbound-in-scope engagement is a red flag, not a clean answer. Escalate it to their legal or compliance owner before build.

Source system for campaign lists, and how results get written back.
For agentless campaigns: what message goes out, on what trigger, and what happens when the customer replies, presses a key, or calls the number back?
questions.logic: The callback path is where agentless campaigns break. An outbound reminder that generates inbound volume into an unprepared queue is a self-inflicted service-level event on day one.

questions.text: Do you run, or plan to run, SMS outbound campaigns?
questions.logic: SMS outbound is a distinct workstream from voice dialing: a different consent model, carrier registration, and a separate inbound-reply handling path. Price and scope it on its own.

questions.text: SMS outbound readiness — which are in place today?
options: Inbound-reply routing to an agent or bot
questions.logic: 10DLC/short-code registration and opt-in records gate go-live on SMS campaigns the way CSRs gate number porting. Anything other than "in place" becomes a timeline assumption, not a task.

questions.logic: The binding constraint on Expert Assist value is content quality, not configuration. A low score here converts into a content-remediation workstream, and it is far cheaper to scope that at kickoff than to discover it during UAT.

questions.logic: Some clinical, legal and benefits contexts require certified human interpretation. Establish the boundary before designing around AI interpretation.

questions.logic: Paired with screen recording in the next question — the two are frequently assumed together and licensed separately.

questions.logic: Blended digital channels break single-channel forecasting models. If B2.7 shows blending and C2.1 shows spreadsheets, that combination is a named risk.

questions.logic: The most reliable predictor of WFM adoption failure. A score of 3 or below converts into a change-management task, not a configuration task.

groups.title: Agent desktop, CTI adapters and Agent Mobile

options: Screen pop on caller or intent match

questions.logic: Without a named owner of the target object model, CTI write-back becomes an unassigned dependency that surfaces in UAT. This single question prevents the most common integration slip.

questions.text: Do agents work in VDI or on locked-down endpoints?
options: Yes, restricted browser or managed device
questions.logic: VDI changes media handling, headset support and troubleshooting. Establish it before design, not during pilot.

Mobile use cases:
Mobile device management posture:
questions.logic: BYOD-unmanaged plus PHI or payment data in the interaction is a privacy design question, not a mobility question. Route it into C5.

questions.text: Anything about the agent's physical working environment we should know — clinical floor, warehouse, retail counter, home office, shared space.

groups.title: Surveys and Voice of the Customer

questions.text: Do you run post-interaction surveys today?
How are they collected?
Response rate: ____%  ·  CSAT: ____ (scale ____)  ·  NPS: ____  ·  CES: ____
Current survey or VoC tool, and contract end date.
What should trigger a survey?
questions.logic: Surveying self-service containments is how you find out whether "contained" actually meant "resolved." Most customers have never done it and it is one of the strongest early optimization findings.

questions.text: Closed-loop follow-up on detractors:
Where must survey results land?
Our survey results actually change how we operate.
Which survey questions must be preserved word-for-word, and why?
questions.logic: Benchmark continuity and regulatory wording. Rewriting a question resets the trend line, so capture the untouchables before redesigning the instrument.

groups.title: Data privacy, PII redaction and encryption

questions.text: Which sensitive data types appear in your interactions?

questions.logic: "In the clear" alongside payment card data in C5.1 is an automatic Red on the privacy dimension and a conversation with their compliance owner before build, not after.

questions.text: Encryption-at-rest requirements:
questions.logic: Key management requirements change the deployment model and the timeline. "Not yet defined" on a signed SOW is a gap to close in week one.
